correctness.rationale: The weighted Laplacian decomposes into four orthogonal eigenspaces with eigenvalues \(0,sa+rb,sb+rc,(s+r)b\). Symmetry averaging of \(\lambda_2\), a concave minimum of linear Rayleigh quotients, proves an invariant optimal allocation exists without presupposing all optimizers invariant. Positive homogeneity reduces the optimum to an exact one-dimensional convex piecewise-linear cost. Its slopes on each allowed interval produce the stated \(\tau_1\) and \(\tau_2\), all strict regimes and complete invariant equality intervals. Direct substitution checks budgets and exact spectral gaps. The standalone exact rational checker validates 955 instances and eigenspaces, not the universal theorem by enumeration.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Sun et al. establish concavity, semidefinite optimization and continuous-time graph rates, but do not state the values \(\tau_1=s(r+1)/[r(s-1)]\) and \(\tau_2=2s/(s-1)\) or the counterintuitive phase deleting cheaper B-internal edges first. Their framework motivates rather than states this classification. Boyd et al. establish symmetry averaging in discrete time; these general techniques are credited. Shakeri et al. vary cross-layer links but keep the within-layer weights fixed, a distinct feasible set and different target. The retrieved published graph-invariant records neither state nor logically imply this Laplacian rate-allocation theorem.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text literature supports the general fastest-mixing SDP and symmetry reduction but no explicit two-price three-orbit complete-graph threshold classification was identified. This claim is strictly the closed-form all-size, all-price phase diagram and its cheaper-edge-deletion intermediate regime, not novelty of \(\lambda_2\) optimization, rate budgeting, SDPs, or group averaging. The search is not a proof of historical priority; residual specialized-literature risk is recorded.
residual_risks: An earlier article or monograph might encode the same three-orbit phase diagram through a general exact weighted-complete-graph theorem; text searches and the three inspected primary papers cannot rule that out.

value.rationale: A natural all-to-all two-population diffusion design has an exact and globally optimal topology/rate allocation for all \(s,r\ge2\) and \(t>0\). The distinct two-threshold regime when the costly group is larger proves a non-obvious design phenomenon: expensive internal links remain positive when every cheaper internal link in the other group is dropped. The exact optimal gap and two threshold formulas replace repeated SDP solving and explain comparative-static structure; it is not a random finite slice or textbook restatement.
